answer: Admission to the policy summit requires a unique measured kernel: the agent must remotely attest a distinct code-and-device measurement and keep it live. Each epoch, randomly chosen incumbents send a short-window zephyr challenge that only the attested kernel can sign. Identities that share a measurement, miss the window, or show correlated latency are merged and slashed. A farm cannot mint cheap aliases from one image; it must buy, attest, and staff a separate kernel per fake identity, so a voting bloc costs isolated hardware and always-on operators, not a copied script.
